definition: Rexer Analytics’s Annual Data Miner Survey is the largest survey of data mining, data science, and analytics professionals in the industry.
details: It consists of approximately 50 multiple choice and open-ended questions that cover seven general areas of data mining science and practice: (1) Field and goals, (2) Algorithms, (3) Models, (4) Tools (software packages used), (5) Technology, (6) Challenges, and (7) Future. It is conducted as a service (without corporate sponsorship) to the data mining community, and the results are usually announced at the PAW (Predictive Analytics World) conferences and shared via freely available summary reports. In the 2013 survey, 1259 data miners from 75 countries participated. After 2011, Rexer Analytics moved to a biannual schedule.

explainer.lead: Rexer's Annual Data Miner Survey is the largest survey of data mining, data science, and analytics professionals in the industry. It matters as a broad read on tools, algorithms, and challenges in practice.

tiers.eli5: It is a big yearly questionnaire sent to data scientists to find out what tools they use and what problems they hit.
tiers.practitioner: Analysts use its results to see which software packages and algorithms peers favor and what challenges dominate. A pitfall is treating self-reported survey answers as objective performance data.
tiers.paperLevel: A survey of roughly 50 multiple-choice and open-ended questions covering seven areas: field and goals, algorithms, models, tools, technology, challenges, and future; results are announced at PAW conferences and shared in free summary reports, and it is run without corporate sponsorship.

explainer.example: A team choosing a modeling stack checks the survey's tools section to see which packages are most widely used before committing.
